intended_object: The continuous inclusion of the equator {p ∈ S² : p₃ = 0} of the unit 2-sphere into the twice-punctured sphere S² \ {N, S}. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: `sphere2Equator` is the subtype of points of the unit sphere in E3 whose third coordinate is zero. `sphere2PunctureIntersection` is the open subset of the sphere obtained by intersecting the complement of the north pole with the complement of the south pole. The underlying function `sphere2EquatorToPunctureIntersectionPoint` keeps the point p unchanged: it only proves that p is neither pole, since a pole has third coordinate ±1 and p has third coordinate 0. Continuity comes from continuity of `Subtype.val` followed by `subtype_mk`. So the definition is exactly the subspace inclusion. The library uses it as one half of the deformation retraction of the twice-punctured sphere onto the equator; the other half is the projection `sphere2PunctureIntersectionToEquator`. This is one specific map between specific spaces, so being concrete is not a matter of being too narrow. Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this map; in general it would be an instance of `Subtype.val` / the subspace inclusion.
